title: Electrowetting-based Digital Microfluidics Platform for Automated Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay
protocol: Conduct all preliminary steps in a sterile environment to avoid contaminations.
Prepare running buffer (100 mM HEPES, pH 7.5) using 4-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine-1-ethanesulfonic acid and add Tween 80 to a concentration of 0.01% (v/v).
Aliquot 0.2 mL of NHS-activated magnetic microbeads into a plastic tube.
Remove the supernatant from the beads.
Wash the beads with 1 mL of ice-cold 1 mM HCl.
Bind selected antibody at 40 μg/mL in 67 mM Borate Buffer to the beads for 1 h with shaking at 37 °C.
Wash unbound antibodies twice with 0.8 mL of Elution Buffer.
Quench the reaction with 1 mL of Quenching Buffer for 1 h.
Wash the beads once with Modified Borate Buffer and once with IP Lysis/Wash Buffer.
Resuspend the beads in 0.5 mL of IP Lysis/Wash Buffer.
Store the resuspended beads at 4 °C until required for use.
Couple microbeads to the antibodies the day before EWOD-isolation and ELISA on-chip.
Block the microbeads coupled with antibody overnight using final concentration 4 mg/mL for the microbeads in Blocker Casein (1% w/v) in 100 mM PBS.
Separate beads from Blocker Casein using a magnet, remove supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL running buffer and mix for 1 min.
Repeat washing steps twice to reduce bead adhesion to the surface and facilitate droplet movement.
Resuspend beads in running buffer at a concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Prepare neutravidin conjugated HRP solution to a final concentration of 1 μg/mL in Running Buffer.
Prepare biotinylated secondary antibody solution to a final concentration of 1 μg/mL in Running Buffer.
Draw the design of the electrodes and connectors in 2D using standard CAD software.
Include also the waste collection pad with dimensions of 5 x 5 mm² to store the used solvents.
Send the design drawing to a mask manufacturing service for printing the chromium mask onto a glass substrate.
Cut the plate to size of 56 x 56 mm² with a precision CNC Dicing/Cutting Saw.
Stick masking tape over the electrical contacts to isolate them.
Coat the chromium-glass plate with a dielectric layer by depositing 6 µm Parylene-C using the Gorham process with 7.4 g of DPX-C in a Parylene Deposition System.
Spin-coat amorphous fluoropolymers using a spin-coater at 1500 rpm for 30 s on top of the plate and bake it at 140 °C for 30 min.
Remove the masking tape from the electrical contacts.
Spin-coat amorphous fluoropolymers using a spin-coater at 1500 rpm for 30 s on top of the 4-in silicon wafer and bake it at 140 °C for 30 min.
Remove the lid from the DMF platform.
Place a clean actuation plate onto the rotating stage, chromium facing upwards.
Align the actuation plate with the upper left corner of the recessed stage.
Clamp the actuation plate from the top using the panel with the 47 contact pins.
Lay the 0.5 mm shim and the 2 mm polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) separator onto the rotating stage.
Aliquot four 2.5-µl droplets of Running buffer onto the B-, A-, R-, E-denoted pads, one droplet on each pad.
Aliquot 2.5 µl of Luminol:H2O2 (1:1, v/v) solution onto the D-denoted pad.
Aliquot 2.5 µl of Neutravidin conjugated to HRP (1 μg/mL) onto the F-denoted pad.
Aliquot 2.5 µl of Biotinylated secondary antibody (1 μg/mL) onto the G-denoted pad.
Aliquot 2.5 µl of Microbeads with conjugated primary antibody (2.5 mg/mL) onto the I-denoted pad.
Aliquot 2.5 µL of the unknown sample onto C-denoted pad.
Place the cover plate on the surface of the rig beside the round recess area.
Slide the cover plate laterally into the recess and place it on top of the actuation plate.
Put the permanent magnet on top of the cover plate and secure it by sliding the two latches.
Rotate the stage by 180° and inspect visually if the loaded droplets are still in place.
Remove the magnet and the cover plate if a droplet is displaced.
Recover the displaced droplet with a clean pipette and place it again on the loading pad.
Check that the loading position for each droplet matches the programmed actuation sequence in the software.
Dismount the photodetector to visually check the position of the droplets.
Position the photodetector screened "can" into the slot of the rotating stage.
Connect the cable to the photodetector screened "can".
Place the lid over the DMF platform and start the program sequence using the software interface developed at the University of Hertfordshire.

Ensure that the programmed sequence prompt messages appear at the interface to inform the operator that "The luminol droplet is ready to collect the extracted magnetic beads" or "The detection droplet is ready to be moved to the detection site".
Require confirmation from the operator to proceed with the sequence.
Start the program sequence using the software interface.
Mount the photodetector screened "can" into the slit of the rotating stage, when prompted.
Connect the cable to the photodetector screened "can", by inserting the pins in the socket.
Place the lid over the DMF platform and resume the assay.
Use additional software for reading and recording luminescence from the droplet as a function of time in a CSV file.
Remove liquid waste and clean the chip.
Ensure equipment is switched off and disconnected from power sources prior to cleaning.
Wear gloves, a lab coat, and goggles protective glass (PPE) when removing biological samples from the chip.
Open the DMF platform lid.
Rotate the stage 180°.
Unhinge the magnet casing.
Remove the magnet from the rotating stage and place it onto the bench.
Remove the cover plate, silicon wafer, from the slit with a pair of tweezers.
Rinse the wafer with DI water.
Dry the wafer with compressed air.
Place the wafer in a Petri dish for storage and reuse.
Use a micropipette to move liquid waste from the pad without touching the surface.
Clean the surface by wicking off the liquid from the actuation plate using absorbent paper.
Sweep gently the surface of the electrodes with a clean DI water droplet using a clean pipette.
Remove the droplet with wicking paper.
